title: placeOrder consumes a stock reservation without returning the units it did not sell — permanent stock leak
detail: placeOrder accepts a reservation whenever it holds AT LEAST the ordered quantity of every ordered line (checkout.ts:671-682: `useReservation = [...wanted].every(([k, qty]) => (held.get(k) ?? 0) >= qty)`), then marks it `status: 'consumed'` (checkout.ts:966-968) and never reconciles the surplus. Any unit the reservation was holding that the order did not consume — a whole line the customer dropped, or the difference after a quantity reduction — is left decremented from `products.stock` / `variants[].stock` with no owner. `stockReservationSweep` only restores reservations whose status is still 'active' (functions/src/scheduled/sweeps.ts:132-143), and `releaseStock` returns early for a non-'active' reservation (functions/src/orders/reservations.ts:256), so nothing ever gives those units back. This is reachable because the web checkout page reserves exactly once per mount (web/src/app/(shop)/checkout/page.tsx:120-153 — `reserveStartedRef` blocks re-entry even though the effect lists `linesCount` as a dependency) while its cart is a LIVE mirror of `customers/{uid}.cart` (web/src/lib/cart.ts:262-281), which the Flutter app and any second tab write to. The app re-reserves on every bag change (app/lib/features/checkout/checkout_screen.dart:142-149) but it too holds a fixed reservation while the Payment screen is open (app/lib/features/checkout/payment_screen.dart:157).
failure_scenario: Product A has stock 5, product B has stock 1. Customer's bag = A×1, B×1. They open /checkout on the desktop web: reserveStock takes both (A=4, B=0). While the page is open they remove B from the bag on their phone; the web cart store receives the customer-doc snapshot and `lines` becomes [A×1]. They press Place order — placeOrder is called with lines=[A×1] and the original reservationId, `held={A:1,B:1} ⊇ wanted={A:1}` so useReservation is true, the reservation is flipped to 'consumed', and B's single unit stays subtracted from stock forever. B now reads 0 in the storefront and in the admin Inventory list and can never be sold again until an admin notices and runs a manual Adjust stock. The same happens with quantities: reserve A×3, reduce to A×1 before placing, 2 units are lost.
fix: In the placeOrder transaction, when `useReservation` is true, compute `surplus = held − wanted` per (productId, variantId) and add it back to `products.stock` / `variants[].stock` in the same per-product write that bumps soldCount (reuse `restoreReservedStock` from reservations.ts, which is already written for exactly this shape). Cheap belt-and-braces on the client: make the web checkout page re-run `callReserveStock` whenever the cart signature (line key + qty) changes, the way app/lib/features/checkout/checkout_screen.dart:144 already does.

title: Admin 'Cancelled' is a one-click, unconfirmed, irreversible refund + restock
detail: `onSetStatus` (OrderDetailPage.tsx:92-103) fires `changeOrderStatus` the instant a status is picked from the dropdown, with no confirmation dialog and no note field. For `status === 'cancelled'` the server runs the full money path — `performCancellation` restocks every line, credits `amountPaidPaise` to the customer's wallet with an immutable walletTransactions row, releases the coupon, reverses the affiliate commission and settles the payment row (functions/src/orders/cancel.ts:104-234). `cancelled` is terminal in the transition graph (functions/src/orders/status.ts:15-23), so there is no undo. Every other money-moving action in the admin is behind a ConfirmDialog that spells out the consequence (admin/src/features/returns/routes/ReturnsListPage.tsx:226-251), and both storefronts confirm before cancelling (web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/page.tsx:279-309, app/lib/features/orders/order_detail_screen.dart:201-218).
failure_scenario: An operator on an 'accepted' order opens 'Update status' intending 'Packing' (the first menu entry) and clicks one row lower onto 'Cancelled'. The order is cancelled immediately: stock is returned, a spin coupon is un-burned, a pending affiliate commission is reversed, and for a prepaid order the full `amountPaidPaise` is credited to the customer's wallet as a permanent ledger entry. Nothing in the admin can reverse any of it — the wallet credit can only be clawed back by a manual wallet adjustment, and the order can never leave 'cancelled'.
fix: Gate the 'cancelled' branch of `onSetStatus` behind the existing ConfirmDialog, stating the amount that will be refunded and the units that will be restocked, and pass the operator's reason through as `note` so `cancellationReason` is not always the generic 'Cancelled by admin'.

title: Cancellation does not invalidate the published invoice — the customer keeps a tax invoice billing the full amount
detail: `performCancellation`'s order update (cancel.ts:227-234) writes status/cancelledAt/reason/paymentStatus and nothing else: `invoiceUrl` and `invoiceGeneratedAt` are left pointing at the Storage object rendered at placement, which prints 'Tax Invoice', the full `totalPaise` as Total, and 'Payment: cod · pending' (functions/src/orders/invoice.ts:70-82). That object is publicly reachable by its download token, and both storefronts still link it: web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/invoice/page.tsx:108-113 renders a 'Download PDF' button whenever `order.invoiceUrl` is set, and the app shares/links the same URL (app/lib/features/orders/invoice_screen.dart:55-58). The admin code already knows the document is stale after a cancel — admin/src/features/orders/routes/OrderDetailPage.tsx:137-139 computes `staleAfterCancel` and regenerates instead of reopening — but that only happens if an operator manually opens that order and clicks Invoice. Compounding it, both in-app invoice views print `amountPaidPaise || totalPaise` as 'Total paid' (web invoice/page.tsx:103, app invoice_screen.dart:231), so a cancelled COD order (amountPaidPaise 0) reads 'Total paid ₹1,050' with no cancelled/refunded marking.
failure_scenario: A COD order of ₹1,050 is placed; placeOrder publishes invoices/#BRK-48001.html immediately (checkout.ts:1077-1080). The customer cancels from the app; stock is restored and the order goes to 'cancelled'. They open Account → Orders → Invoice on the web and download a document headed 'Tax Invoice' for ₹1,050 against a cancelled order. Nothing on the page or in the file says it was cancelled or refunded. Used for a reimbursement claim or a chargeback, that document contradicts the store's own books.
fix: In `performCancellation`, either clear `invoiceUrl`/`invoiceGeneratedAt` on the order, or call `generateInvoiceForOrder` after the transaction (it overwrites the same Storage path) and have the renderer print a 'CANCELLED — Credit note' header plus the refunded amount when `order.status === 'cancelled'`. Also drive the two invoice screens' 'Total paid' from paymentStatus rather than `amountPaidPaise || totalPaise`.

title: Web storefront has no out-of-stock handling at the product card or in the bag, so checkout dead-ends
detail: `ProductCard.onAdd` (ProductCard.tsx:28-43) adds to the bag with no stock check at all and blindly picks `product.variants?.[0]` regardless of that variant's stock, then toasts success. The bag page is equally stock-blind: it renders every line through `QtyStepper` with no maximum (web/src/app/(shop)/bag/page.tsx:88-96; web/src/components/checkout/QtyStepper.tsx has no cap prop), shows no per-line availability, and leaves 'Proceed to checkout' permanently enabled (bag/page.tsx:138-140). The only guard is `reserveStock` failing on the checkout page, which toasts and `router.replace('/bag')` (checkout/page.tsx:139-145) — straight back to a bag that still contains the unsellable line, with no indication which one it is. The Flutter app does all three: the card turns into an inert marker when `!product.inStock` and picks the first IN-STOCK variant (app/lib/core/widgets/product_card.dart:284-311), and the bag's checkout bar watches live stock and blocks with 'Out of stock' (app/lib/features/cart/bag_screen.dart:353-375).
failure_scenario: Product 'Attar 12ml' has variants [Small: stock 0, Large: stock 4]. On the web home rail the customer taps the + on the card: the Small (sold-out) variant is added and a green 'added to bag' toast is shown. The bag shows the line normally and lets them raise the quantity to 5. 'Proceed to checkout' → reserveStock throws failed-precondition, a toast fires and they are bounced back to the bag, unchanged. Pressing checkout again repeats it forever; the customer has no way to learn that it is the Small variant that is unavailable, and the Large variant they could have bought never gets sold.
fix: Disable/replace the quick-add button when `!inStock(product)` (the predicate already exists at web/src/components/catalog/ListingView.tsx:24-27) and select the first in-stock variant instead of `variants[0]`; in the bag, resolve live stock per line (the app's `watchLineStock` shape) to cap the stepper, badge unavailable lines and disable 'Proceed to checkout' — mirroring app/lib/features/cart/bag_screen.dart.

title: App return-request screen promises a wallet credit even when auto-refund to wallet is off
detail: The info box shown while raising a return states unconditionally: 'Approved refunds are credited to your Normal Wallet within 24 hours.' When `settings/returns.autoRefundToWallet` is false, `adminApproveOrderRequest` deliberately moves NO money: it forces `refundMethod: 'gateway'`, leaves `refundedAt`/`refundTransactionId` null and writes no walletTransactions row (functions/src/returns/decisions.ts:113-153). Every other surface is honest about this — the admin list/drawer/confirm dialog use `plannedRefundTargetLabel` and say 'you must pay it back to their original payment method yourself' (admin/src/features/returns/api/returns.ts:64-67, ReturnsListPage.tsx:238-245, 355-361), and the app's own order-detail return card branches on `isRefundedToWallet` to say 'will be refunded to your original payment method' (app/lib/features/orders/order_detail_screen.dart:541-553). Only the screen where the customer commits to the return makes the unconditional promise, and the pending-state line at order_detail_screen.dart:557 repeats it.
failure_scenario: The store runs with 'Auto-refund to wallet' off (refunds are pushed back through Razorpay by hand). A customer returns a ₹1,200 item from the app, is told the money lands in their Normal Wallet within 24 hours, and checks the wallet the next day: balance unchanged, no transaction. They raise a support ticket / chargeback for a refund that is in fact owed and simply queued for a manual payout.
fix: Read `settings/returns.autoRefundToWallet` on this screen (the repository already reads `settings/returns` for windowDays — app/lib/features/orders/data/orders_repository.dart:58-66) and switch the copy to 'refunded to your original payment method' when it is false; do the same for the pending-state line at order_detail_screen.dart:557.

title: Web order summary and invoice double-count the spin reward as a second discount
detail: `placeOrder` derives `spinRewardPaise` FROM the coupon discount rather than in addition to it: `spinRewardPaise = userCouponId && userCouponSource === 'spin' ? Math.max(0, discountPaise) : 0` and the same value is stored as `discountPaise` (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:541-542, 884-886). So on a spin-coupon order `order.discountPaise === order.spinRewardPaise`. The web order-detail payment summary renders BOTH as separate reductions (page.tsx:157-162) and the web invoice adds both into one savings figure: `const savings = order.discountPaise + order.spinRewardPaise + order.walletUsedPaise` (web/src/app/(shop)/account/orders/[id]/invoice/page.tsx:54). The Flutter app hit and fixed exactly this — app/lib/features/orders/data/order.dart:187-200 documents that adding both 'double-counted the discount and stopped the invoice reconciling to Total paid' and exposes `discountsExWalletPaise = discountPaise` alone (used at order_detail_screen.dart:409-414).
failure_scenario: Customer wins a ₹200 spin coupon and places an order: subtotal ₹2,000, discount ₹200, delivery ₹0, wallet ₹0, total ₹1,800. The web order page lists 'Discount −₹200.00' and 'Spin reward −₹200.00' against a 'Total paid ₹1,800.00'; the web invoice prints 'Discounts + wallet −₹400.00' under a ₹2,000 line total and a ₹1,800 total, so the document does not add up (2000 − 400 = 1600 ≠ 1800). The same order in the app shows a single, correct −₹200. A customer comparing the two, or an accountant reconciling the invoice, sees the store's own document contradict itself by the reward amount.
fix: Treat `spinRewardPaise` as a label for `discountPaise`, not an extra reduction: on page.tsx render one row (labelled 'Spin reward' when `spinRewardPaise > 0`, else 'Discount'), and on invoice/page.tsx compute `savings = order.discountPaise + order.walletUsedPaise`. Mirror app/lib/features/orders/data/order.dart:195-204.

title: adminAdjustStock never maintains the top-level products.stock aggregate that the order paths keep decrementing
detail: The two subsystems disagree about what `products.stock` means on a variant product. The order paths treat it as an aggregate over all variants and move it on every variant line: `placeOrder` does `stock: FieldValue.increment(-totalQty)` for variant lines (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:807-815), `reserveStock` the same (functions/src/orders/reservations.ts:211-216, and reservations.ts:23-25 states outright that 'the top-level products.stock counter aggregates every variant'), and `performCancellation` / `restoreReservedStock` increment it back. The admin treats it as dead once variants exist: `saveProduct` zeroes it on conversion and comments that 'every reader stops looking at the top-level stock from then on' (admin/src/features/products/api/products.ts:223-242). `adminAdjustStock` follows the admin view — it only writes `update.stock` when a base (variantId === null) delta is present (inventory.ts:121-128), and the Adjust screen never emits one for a variant product because `buildSkuRows` produces variant rows only (admin/src/features/inventory/api/inventory.ts:225-241). Net: for a variant product `products.stock` starts at 0 and marches negative, one unit per unit sold, and no admin surface can correct it.
failure_scenario: A variant product is created, its variants are stocked to 50 through Adjust stock (variants[].stock = 50, products.stock stays 0), and 30 units sell. The document now reads `stock: -30` while `sum(variants[].stock) = 20`. Nothing user-facing reads the field today (the web, the app, admin Products and admin Inventory are all variant-aware), so there is no visible symptom yet — but the stored field is wrong, the server's own comment claims it is the aggregate, and any future consumer (a Firestore query/order-by on `stock`, an export, a low-stock rule, a new client) will read nonsense.
fix: Pick one contract and enforce it. Either drop the `stock:` increment from placeOrder/reserveStock/cancel/restoreReservedStock for variant lines (making the field genuinely unused when hasVariants), or make `adminAdjustStock` recompute `update.stock` as the sum of the post-adjustment variants array whenever `p.hasVariants` — inventory.ts already has the whole array in hand at line 132.

title: Admin cancel re-validates the status outside the transaction (TOCTOU on the refund path)
detail: The admin cancel branch reads the order with a plain `ref.get()`, checks the transition graph, and then calls `performCancellation` WITHOUT passing `allowedStatuses` (status.ts:64-75). `performCancellation` only rejects an order that is already 'cancelled' (functions/src/orders/cancel.ts:53-58: the `allowedStatuses` guard is skipped when the option is undefined), and before opening its transaction it awaits two extra round trips — the legacy items subcollection read and the commissions query (cancel.ts:35-40). The customer path does pass `allowedStatuses: CANCELLABLE` (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:1156-1162), so only the admin path is unguarded inside the transaction.
failure_scenario: Order #BRK-48120 is 'packed'. Admin A opens it and clicks Update status → Cancelled; the pre-check reads 'packed' and passes. In the ~100-300 ms while performCancellation is doing its two pre-transaction reads, admin B (or a second tab) moves the order to 'shipped'. The cancellation transaction then commits against a shipped order: stock is restored and the customer refunded for goods already with the courier, and the order lands in 'cancelled' with a 'shipped' timeline entry in front of the 'cancelled' one.
fix: Pass `allowedStatuses` through from the admin path — `performCancellation({ ..., allowedStatuses: Object.keys(TRANSITIONS).filter((s) => TRANSITIONS[s].includes('cancelled')) })` — so the graph is re-asserted inside the transaction that moves the money.

title: The stock-adjustment ledger records only admin adjustments, so Stock history cannot be reconciled to on-hand stock
detail: `stockAdjustments` rows are written only by the Adjust stock screen (inventory.ts:165-193). Every other movement of the same counters — placement (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:807-815), checkout reservation and release (functions/src/orders/reservations.ts:110, 211-216), the expiry sweep (functions/src/scheduled/sweeps.ts:153-157) and cancellation restock (functions/src/orders/cancel.ts:125-134) — writes nothing. Within a single row `before + delta === after` does hold (the values come back from the transaction itself, inventory.ts:127/138 and are echoed at inventory.ts:148-153), but consecutive rows do not chain and the newest row's `after` does not match the Inventory figure. StockHistoryModal presents the columns 'Change' and 'After' with no caveat (admin/src/features/inventory/components/StockHistoryModal.tsx:69, 89-94).
failure_scenario: An admin receives 20 units of a SKU (history: +20, After 20). Over the week 17 sell. Inventory now shows 3. The admin opens Stock history to investigate the gap, sees a single row saying 'After 20' and no other entries, and concludes 17 units were stolen or that a save was lost — the sales that actually consumed them are invisible in the ledger the screen presents as the SKU's stock history.
fix: Either rename the column/screen to make clear it is an adjustment log rather than a stock ledger, or write a `stockAdjustments`-shaped row (reason: 'Order placed' / 'Order cancelled' / 'Return to inventory') from the server paths that move stock, so the ledger chains and reconciles to the live figure.

title: A cancelled order permanently consumes the customer's first-order eligibility
detail: `placeOrder` increments `stats.ordersCount` and `stats.totalSpentPaise` at placement (functions/src/orders/checkout.ts:832-833). `performCancellation` increments `stats.ordersCancelled` but reverses neither (cancel.ts:138-149). `stats.ordersCount` is the gate for `firstOrderOnly` coupons in both the pre-check and the in-transaction re-assertion (checkout.ts:252-259 and 747-749), for the 'existing customers' coupon audience (checkout.ts:198-205), and for the spin campaign's new/returning audience split (functions/src/spin/execute.ts:97-106). It is also the 'Orders' column in the admin Customers list (admin/src/features/customers/routes/CustomersListPage.tsx:125).
failure_scenario: A new customer places a COD order, then cancels it five minutes later because they picked the wrong size. `stats.ordersCount` is now 1 and never comes back down. They re-place the order and the WELCOME10 coupon (firstOrderOnly) is rejected with 'This coupon is for first orders only.', and a 'new users' spin campaign no longer offers them anything — even though they have never completed a purchase. The admin Customers list also shows them as having 1 order with a lifetime spend that includes the fully refunded amount.
fix: Decrement `stats.ordersCount` and `stats.totalSpentPaise` by the cancelled order's total inside `performCancellation`'s customer update (it is already writing that document), keeping `stats.ordersCancelled` as the separate lifetime tally. If 'orders ever placed' is the intended meaning of ordersCount, gate `firstOrderOnly` and the spin audience on `ordersDelivered` instead.

title: A cancelled COD order's payment row is marked 'failed', inflating the admin's failed-payment count and disagreeing with the order
detail: `performCancellation` settles the payment row as `refundPaise > 0 ? 'refunded' : 'failed'` (cancel.ts:219-224). For a plain COD order nothing was ever collected, so `amountPaidPaise` is 0 and the row becomes 'failed'. Meanwhile the ORDER's paymentStatus is left as-is — `refundPaise > 0 ? 'refunded' : (o.paymentStatus ?? 'pending')` (cancel.ts:232) — so it stays 'pending'. The admin Payments page counts `statusOf(p) === 'failed'` into its header stat and renders a red 'Failed' badge (admin/src/features/payments/routes/PaymentsListPage.tsx:43-53, 166-175), while `effectivePaymentStatus` only upgrades pending COD rows for DELIVERED orders and therefore does not special-case cancelled ones (admin/src/features/payments/api/payments.ts:46-51). The admin Orders list, reading the order, still shows a gold 'COD' pill for the same order (admin/src/features/orders/api/orders.ts:63-65).
failure_scenario: Ten COD orders are cancelled by customers in a month. The Payments header reads '₹X this month · 10 failed' and ten rows show a red 'Failed' badge, which reads as ten gateway/collection failures needing investigation. Opening any of them and clicking 'View order' shows an order whose Payment status is 'COD / pending', not failed. There were no payment failures at all.
fix: Introduce a 'cancelled' payment status (or reuse 'refunded' only when money moved and leave an uncollected COD row at 'pending' while the order is cancelled), and teach `effectivePaymentStatus`/`paymentStatusPill` to render a cancelled order's payment as 'Cancelled' rather than 'Failed'. Keep the order's paymentStatus and the payment row in agreement in both cases.
